details: The sole run-codex-row Popen invokes codex exec once and never invokes the documented codex exec resume surface.
The bootstrap ends its first turn with an active Goal and assumes the noninteractive exec process will autonomously begin a later native Goal continuation turn.
No official OpenAI documentation or durable local direct-exec example establishes that automatic second-turn behavior for this exact surface.
Static and mutation checks simulate the later turn; they do not prove the runtime transition.
The subject is therefore never launch-authorized under this exact implementation. Its exact tool-output prompt framing also remains empirically unproven.

established.claim: A Goal is attached to the active task while work continues across turns.
codex exec resume continues a saved exec session and accepts an optional follow-up prompt, including stdin via '-'.

not_established: Automatic later Goal continuation inside a single noninteractive codex exec process after its first turn ends.
A documented internal create_goal restoration receipt for that unresumed process.

requirements: Create one fresh persisted Codex exec task with a bootstrap containing no scored subject bytes.
Require exact get_goal-null, create_goal-active, and get_goal-active evidence in the activation turn.
After the first process exits, independently attest the active Goal in durable rollout and Goal database state.
Resume the exact same task ID with a non-scored continuation bootstrap.
Inside the resumed turn, require get_goal to return the same active Goal before opening the one-use subject channel.
Release the exact subject bytes only after that resumed-turn Goal evidence is durable.
Require update_goal-complete and a terminal Goal receipt after subject work.
Reject task or Goal reuse, retries, relaunches, replacements, and any prompt leakage before activation.
